events.title: Baghdad Surrenders to the Mongols
events.description: After a siege by the army of Hulegu Khan, the last Abbasid caliph surrendered Baghdad. The Mongols then sacked the city, and hundreds of thousands of people were killed.
events.significance: The fall of Baghdad ended the Abbasid Caliphate's rule and marked the end of the city's golden age as the center of the Islamic world.

events.title: Treaty of Paris Ends the Seven Years' War
events.description: Britain, France and Spain signed the Treaty of Paris. It ended the French and Indian War, and France gave Quebec and most of its North American territory to Britain.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the map of North America and made Britain the dominant colonial power there. It also set the stage for tensions that led to the American Revolution.

events.title: Queen Victoria Marries Prince Albert
events.description: Queen Victoria married her cousin, Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, in a ceremony at the Chapel Royal in St James's Palace, London.
events.significance: The marriage was a famously devoted partnership. Albert became an influential adviser to the Queen and helped shape the monarchy and Victorian-era Britain.

events.title: Deep Blue Defeats Garry Kasparov
events.description: IBM's Deep Blue supercomputer beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov in the first game of their match in Philadelphia. It was the first time a computer had won a game against a reigning world champion under standard tournament conditions.
events.significance: The win was a landmark moment for artificial intelligence. It prompted a public debate about the abilities of machines and foreshadowed Deep Blue's full match victory in 1997.
